headline: I started an 'Abuse Prevention Committee' for my neighborhood WhatsApp group, and now we only use 18th-century courtly French to discuss missing garbage trucks
body:
It all started when I decided that the local level of discourse in our residential complex was becoming far too common. After reading about the high-level concerns regarding decorum, I decided to take charge of our group chat. If a neighbor now wants to complain that the garbage collector missed their lane, they are required to submit their grievance in the form of a formal, poetic letter in French, or face immediate removal by our newly formed 'Tone Oversight Board.'

I admit, it has made resolving mundane issues quite tedious. Last Tuesday, when the water supply was cut, a neighbor tried to send a simple message about his shower being dry. I had to reject it twice because he used the informal 'tu' instead of the polite 'vous' when addressing the society secretary. We eventually spent three hours discussing the conjugations of the verb 'to rinse' before anyone actually bothered to call the plumber.

Some of the older residents have complained that they can no longer report stray dogs or street light outages because they don't have a reliable French-English dictionary handy. I tell them that civilization is a fragile thing, and if we allow one 'arrey bhai' to slip through the cracks, we are only one step away from total anarchy. My neighbors now mostly just use the group to post pictures of their indoor plants, which is perfectly fine by me—as long as they caption them in a way that respects the dignity of the flora.
caption: Nothing says 'civilized society' like a 4-hour grammar debate over a broken sewage pipe. We are bringing back the Renaissance, one passive-aggressive emoji at a time. #WhatsAppEtiquette #SocietyLife #Gentility #India (satire)
